commons.title: Spruce root hat, Chugash - Etholén collection, Museum of Cultures (Helsinki) - DSC04923.JPG
commons.description:
Exhibit in the Arvid Adolf Etholén collection, Museum of Cultures, Helsinki, Finland. Photography was permitted in the museum without restriction. Spruce root hat. The crown is on close plain twining, the sturdier raised twining on the brim forms a whirl pattern. The brim is finished with braiding painted in reddish brown. The hat is painted blue-green all over, with an unidentified imitation of Tlingit totemic design in yellow, red and black on the crown. The edge of the brim, the “seam” between the brim and the crown, and the crown are decorated with clusters of white, red, blue and black glass beads, also used to accentuate the groups of dentalia covering the hat. Two black velvet ribbons lined and trimmed with cotton fabric are sewn to the hoop inside the hat and stitched together under the chin. At the ears, they are hung with pendants comprising 12 dentalia and glass beads.
This hat is probably the one spruce root hat documented as Chugach Eskimo in the Etholén collection of 1846. Holmberg (1855) mentions that in 1850 the Koniag reserved their old spruce root hats for kayak trips; otherwise they had already started to wear (European-style) visor caps. The decoration of trade beads and dentalia, the coloring and the design which differs from Tlingit formline painting show that this valuable hat is of Alutiiq origin, as confirmed also by Holm (1995) who further thinks it might be specifically from Kodiak Island.
commons.editorial_reason: Description specifically attributes the spruce-root hat to Chugach/Alutiiq origin, and the image clearly shows the traditional decorated craft object.
